newsitem.title: USA: Clinton see chance for stable, long-term growth.
newsitem.headline: Clinton see chance for stable, long-term growth.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said in an interview broadcast on Sunday that he was "a little" concerned about the economy slowing down, but that his bet was that a period of stable, long-term growth may be possible.

Asked on ABC's "This Week with David Brinkley" programme whether he was concerned about the economy slowing, Clinton replied: "A little bit. But let me say if you look at the pattern of it over the last four or five years, from quarter to quarter ... the growth rate will vary."

On October 30 the government reported that gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 2.2 percent in the third quarter, a respectable performance but a marked slowing from the second quarter's 4.7 percent rise.

"If we can keep the interest rates down with the deficit reduction package and a balanced budget, keep investing in education and technology and keep expanding trade, I'm not sure we'll be as victimised by the business cycle as we have been in the past," Clinton added.
"We may be able to have much more stable and much longer term growth than we ever had before. That's my bet," he said. "I believe this new economy may give us a chance for a new period of growth."
The interview was taped on Friday.
